playlist.name: Yes Essentials
playlist.description: Yes didn't invent progressive rock, but they helped bring it to mainstream audiences, steering the development and definition of the genre. Once their classic lineup of Jon Anderson, Chris Squire, Steve Howe, Rick Wakeman and Bill Bruford locked into place for 1971's 'Fragile,' the band crystallized all of the sonic and visual signifiers that eventually became synonymous with prog rock. Yes shifted between complicated time signatures, spliced pastoral folk and Baroque classical in their muscular rock & roll, structured their songs as mini-suites, and wrapped the entire package in fantastical artwork by Roger Dean. This early incarnation of Yes didn't last long, and once the band regrouped in the late '70s, they embraced the steely, shiny sounds of album-oriented rock. They soared through the MTV era on the strength of their 1983 album '90125' and its dazzling, Trevor Horn-produced hit "Owner of a Lonely Heart," the band's first American No. 1 hit. Yes' fame had diminished somewhat by the end of the '80s, but the band remained active throughout the next decade and beyond, albeit amid multiple line-up changes and hiatuses. They maintained a loyal fan base through touring and the sporadic release of new albums. (Bio: Rovi / Photo: Michael Putland/Getty Images)

playlist.name: The Beatles Essentials
playlist.description:
In the illustrious history of popular music and rock 'n' roll alike, there has simply never been a bigger band, nor one more beloved or influential, than The Beatles. Formed 1960 in Liverpool, England around the massive pillars of John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr, the Fab Four grew from overnight pop sensation to the most respected and pioneering artists of their craft. In less than a decade, The Beatles released 13 groundbreaking studio albums, compiling a legendary music catalogue unlike anything the world has seen before or after. More than any compilation has been able to contain, this definitive playlist gathers all the greatest songs from the greatest band of all time. 
(Photo: Universal)

playlist.name: Remember...the 1960s
playlist.description: From manicured crooners to freak-flag-waving hippies: the years between 1960 and 1969 were perhaps the most revolutionary and influential modern culture has ever seen. It was a time when the pop charts and the alternative charts were one and the same. In a rainbow of genres and styles, it was a period of unprecedented and unrepeated innovation - the results as timeless as anything that’s been created since. So much of this music still lives strong in the popular consciousness, reaching out to new generations. The ‘60s were a time of such optimism and idealism, progress and change, the biggest disappointment was when the trajectory of that rocket didn’t last. These are some of the biggest hits and most memorable moments from a golden era. (Cover: Connie Francis (1937-2025), /  Photo: UMG, press)

playlist.name: Genesis Essentials
playlist.description: Formed in Surrey in 1967, Genesis have explored a wide spectre of genres throughout their musical career. Moving from folk music to progressive rock during the ‘70s, before leaning towards a more commercial pop-sound during the height of their fame in the ‘80s. Though the band originally featured Peter Gabriel as lead singer, the longest lasting line-up consisted of Phil Collins on drums and vocals, bassist and guitarist Mike Rutherford and keyboardist Tony Banks. (Photo: Rovi)
